findings.title: CrowdStrike to Acquire Zscaler, Bringing Network Security and Zero Trust to the Falcon Platform
findings.summary_md: CrowdStrike's own release announced a definitive all-stock agreement valuing Zscaler at approximately 43.9 billion dollars, with 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share, an implied 260.41 dollars per share based on CrowdStrike's November 20 close and a 34 percent premium. It says Zscaler shareholders will hold about 15.9 percent of the combined company and that closing is expected in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. The release describes a single platform with one data layer and one contract after closing, built on more than 2,000 shared customers and 16 integrations, and says Zscaler protects 50 percent of the Fortune 500 through more than 200 service locations. CrowdStrike projects about 1 billion dollars in annualized run-rate revenue synergies by 30 months after close.

findings.title: CrowdStrike Is in Talks to Buy Cybersecurity Firm Zscaler
findings.summary_md: Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that CrowdStrike was in talks to acquire Zscaler in a deal that would rank among the largest in cybersecurity and create a combined market value of about 265 billion dollars. The report said deliberations were ongoing with no certainty of a transaction, and that neither company immediately commented. It put Zscaler's market value at 32 billion dollars and CrowdStrike's at about 233 billion dollars, noting CrowdStrike's Falcon focus on endpoint security.

findings.title: CrowdStrike in talks to acquire Zscaler, sources say
findings.summary_md: Reuters reported, citing two people familiar with the matter, that CrowdStrike was in talks to buy Zscaler and that discussions might end without an agreement. It noted Zscaler's roughly 32 billion dollar market capitalization, a 17 percent after-hours share jump for Zscaler and an 8 percent drop for CrowdStrike. The report said a combination would fill CrowdStrike's network security gap, compete more directly with Palo Alto Networks, and likely need the backing of founder Jay Chaudhry, who remains Zscaler's largest shareholder. Reuters credited Bloomberg with first reporting the discussions.

findings.title: CrowdStrike, Zscaler Merger Would Create Cybersecurity Giant
findings.summary_md: Investor's Business Daily reported that a CrowdStrike acquisition of Zscaler would create a company with a combined market value of about 265 billion dollars. It said any transaction would likely be mostly stock because CrowdStrike ended July with about 5 billion dollars of cash, and it noted the share reaction to the Bloomberg report.
